mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1300 units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1300, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, indicating a tight labor market, wage pressures increase, leading to higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between increasing industrial production (INDPRO) and rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broadening economic expansion, boosting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns during joint expansions are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a single month signals decreased consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical impact of consumption shocks on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS declines > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL), indicating a tightening monetary policy, S&P 500 returns become negative over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > CPIAUCSL, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: the level of payroll employment (PAYEMS) consistently predicts S&P 500 returns, with higher employment levels leading to positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between PAYEMS and SPX
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly correlated with PAYEMS levels (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Regime-conditional signal: during late-cycle expansions, a GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 3% signals sustained economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of late-cycle instances when GDPC1 > 3%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
